items.description: Sec. 2 says only 'An open domain with some volume fraction f is to be designed on'. The domain's shape and side lengths appear only in Fig. 1. Sec. 5.1 says dataset samples use a 64×64 square domain, but the text never says Fig. 1 is a dataset sample; it is a generic illustration in Sec. 2.
readings: Square domain, L = H (consistent with the 64×64 dataset samples)
Rectangle with L = 2H (cantilever-style illustration)
Rectangle with L = 3H (MBB/beam-style illustration)

items.entity: Finite-element grid for the Fig. 1 example
items.description: No discretization is given for the Fig. 1 example. Only the Sec. 5.1 dataset is described as a '64×64 domain of square elements'. The filter radius of 2.0 is effectively in element units, so the resolution changes the relative minimum feature size.
readings: 64 × 64 square bilinear elements (dataset resolution)
Grid matching a non-square Fig. 1 domain, e.g. 128 × 64 for a 2:1 domain
A higher-resolution grid for the illustration, e.g. 128 × 128

items.description: Sec. 2 and the Fig. 1 caption mention only 'a specific combination of boundary condition ∂Ω_D'. Where it is and how far it extends are shown only in the figure. The Sec. 5.1 dataset picks 1–4 of 16 options (4 corner points, 4 mid-side points, 8 half-edges between them), but the text does not say which ones Fig. 1 uses.
readings: Entire left edge fixed (x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ H; both left half-edges)
One half-edge only, e.g. x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ 0.5H
Two corner points fixed, e.g. (0,0) and (L,0)
A corner point plus a mid-side point, e.g. (0,0) and (0,0.5H)

items.entity: Application point of load P in Fig. 1
items.description: The position of P is shown only in Fig. 1. Sec. 5.1 says only that dataset loads act on 'a random element along the boundary'.
readings: Right edge at mid-height (x = L, y = 0.5H)
Right edge, bottom corner (x = L, y = 0)
Right edge, top corner (x = L, y = H)
Top or bottom edge at mid-span (x = 0.5L)

items.entity: Direction of load P in Fig. 1
items.description: The direction of P is shown only in Fig. 1. If Fig. 1 follows the dataset (Sec. 5.1), the angle is one of '6 evenly distributed values' from 0 to 2π. That phrase is itself ambiguous: it could mean 60° steps that exclude 2π, or linspace including 2π, which gives only 5 distinct directions 72° apart. The text also does not state the reference axis, the sense of rotation, or whether y points up or down (image rows). A vertical load would not be in the 60°-step set.
readings: Vertically downward (−90°), as in a typical schematic
One of 0°, 60°, 120°, 180°, 240°, 300° measured from +x
One of 0°, 72°, 144°, 216°, 288° measured from +x (linspace with 0 ≡ 2π)

items.description: Sec. 2 gives only the symbol P. Only the dataset loads in Sec. 5.1 are stated to have 'unit magnitude'.
readings: Any other value of |P|

items.entity: How load P is applied to the nodes
items.description: Sec. 5.1 assigns the load to a boundary 'element', but places supports on 'nodes'. The text does not say whether P is a single nodal force or is spread over the element's nodes; Fig. 1 shows only an arrow.
readings: Concentrated force on one node of the chosen boundary element (e.g. a node on its outer edge)
Force split equally between the two nodes on the element's boundary edge
Force split equally over all four nodes of the element

items.description: Sec. 2 says only 'some volume fraction f' and gives no value for Fig. 1. Dataset targets range from 30% to 50% (Sec. 5.1); the text does not say whether that range is continuous or a set of discrete values.
readings: Another value in [0.3, 0.5]

items.description: Neither Sec. 2 nor Sec. 5.1 mentions passive regions, and the text does not say whether elements at the load or supports are kept solid.
readings: No passive elements; the whole grid can be designed
Load-application element(s) fixed solid (x = 1)
Elements at the load and at the supports fixed solid

items.description: Sec. 2 leaves E0 as a symbol. Sec. 5.1 uses 'a unit Young's modulus', but states it is 'for the calculation of the finite element fields' (the pre-processing stress and strain-energy fields), not explicitly for the SIMP run.
readings: Another E0 (e.g. a physical value such as 210 GPa)

items.description: Sec. 2 gives no ν. Sec. 5.1 states ν = 0.3 only in the sentence about computing the pre-processing FE fields.
readings: ν = 0.3, also used in the optimization
A different ν in the optimization, e.g. 0.25 or 1/3

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption, thickness and element type
items.description: The text never says whether the model is plane stress or plane strain, gives no out-of-plane thickness, and does not name the element formulation; it says only 'square elements' (Sec. 5.1).
readings: Plane stress, unit thickness, bilinear 4-node quads
Plane strain, bilinear 4-node quads

items.description: Sec. 2 gives E_min only approximately: 'E_min is a small stiffness (~0.001E0)'.
readings: E_min = 1e-3·E0
E_min = 1e-9·E0 (common default, if '~0.001' is read only as 'small')

items.description: Eq. (6) defines w_ei = r_min − |x_i − x_e|, where x_i and x_e are densities in the surrounding text. This conflicts with the usual weight based on the distance between element centres. N_e is never defined. The value r_min = 2.0 appears only in Sec. 5.1 (for the dataset) and has no units.
readings: Standard linear-hat filter: w_ei = max(0, r_min − ‖c_i − c_e‖) on element-centre distances, r_min = 2.0 element widths
Literal Eq. (6): w_ei = r_min − |x_i − x_e| using density differences, with N_e = elements within 2.0 element widths

items.entity: Which density field enters the stiffness and volume
items.description: Eq. (1) and Eq. (4) are written in terms of the design variables x_e. Sec. 2 also says 'Each density x_e is updated by the nearby densities' and the 'design density is then updated to the physical density x̃_e by Eqn. (7)'. It is unclear whether x̃ is used in E_e and V, or whether the filtered field overwrites x at every iteration.
readings: Standard density filter: x̃ enters Eq. (1) and Eq. (4), sensitivities are chain-ruled through the filter, and x stays as the design variable
Filtered field overwrites the design variables every iteration (x ← x̃)
Raw x used in Eq. (1) and Eq. (4); the filter is applied only to sensitivities or updates

items.entity: Optimizer, update rule and stopping criterion
items.description: Sec. 2 says only that 'design variables x_e are updated using the gradient of the compliance'; Sec. 5.1 says 'using a gradient descent algorithm'. The text gives no update scheme, step size or move limit, way of enforcing the volume constraint, convergence tolerance, or iteration limit.
readings: OC update (move limit 0.2, damping 0.5, bisection on the volume multiplier), stop when max|Δx| < 0.01
MMA, stop when max|Δx| < 0.01 or at a fixed iteration cap
Projected steepest descent with a fixed step and volume projection, fixed iteration budget (e.g. 200)

items.description: The starting density distribution is not stated. Sec. 5.1 mentions an 'initial unoptimized domain' (used for the stress and strain-energy fields) but does not give its density.
readings: Uniform x_e = f
Fully solid x_e = 1

items.description: Sec. 2 defines compliance as 'the total strain energy in the system', but Eq. (2) writes c = UᵀKU, which is twice the strain energy.
readings: c = UᵀKU = FᵀU (Eq. 2)
c = ½UᵀKU (total strain energy, as worded)
